                          UNITED STA TES DISTRICT COURT
                       FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
                               ALEXANDRIA DIVISION


 MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

               Plaintiff,

               V.                                            Case No. 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF
                                                             The Honorable Judge
                                                             Rossie D. Alston Jr.


 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,

               Defendants.

 PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR AN ORDER DIRECTING COMPLETION OF THE RULE
             26(0 CONFERENCE AND SUBMISSION OF A DISCOVERY PLAN


        PlaintiffMarvelle J. Ballentine moves under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(f)(l)-(3),

 and under the Court's case-management authority under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16, for

 an order directing the appearing parties to complete the conference Rule 26(f) requires by a date

 certain and to file a written report identifying the parties' agreed proposals and each party's

 separately stated positions on the matters Rule 26(f)(3) requires the discovery plan to address.

 Under Local Civil Rule 7(F), a supporting memorandum, the Declaration ofMarvelle J. Ballentine

 with Exhibits A, B, C-1, and C-2, and a proposed order accompany this Motion.

 I.     GROUNDS
        1.     The action has an operative pleading and appeanng parties. The operative

 pleading is the First Amended Complaint. ECF 5. Defendant National Center for Missing &

 Exploited Children ("NCMEC") appeared on August 12, 2026, ECF 10; Defendant Meta



                                                 1

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 105        Filed 10/28/26      Page 2 of 9 PageID#
                                             1071



 Platforms, Inc. ("Meta") appeared on August 21, 2026, ECF 21; and Defendant Katie Hall

 appeared on September 2, 2026, ECF 45. Each appearance was by motion to dismiss. Those

 motions remain pending. The Doe Defendants have not been identified or served and are not

 participants in the conference.

        2.      Plaintiff transmitted written Rule 26(f) planning materials on October 16, 2026.

 On that date Plaintiff transmitted by electronic mail to counsel of record for each appearing

 Defendant a written Rule 26(£)(2) proposal directed to that Defendant and a common agenda

 addressed to all appearing parties, and requested each Defendant's written response by October

 30, 2026. Ballentine Deel. 11 3-6; Exs. A, B. The materials stated that transmission, expiration of

 the response date, silence, or refusal would not be treated as completion of the conference. Ex. A

 §§ I, IV, V.

        3.      The October 28, 2026 correspondence presents a disagreement about whether

 planning should proceed while the motions to dismiss are pending. On October 28, 2026, Plaintiff

 wrote to counsel for NCMEC and Hall requesting the position of each of those Defendants on

 three subjects: whether it intended to participate in the Rule 26(f) conference; whether it contended

 that any order or other authority excused or postponed its Rule 26(f) obligations; and whether it

 would oppose an order directing the parties to conduct the conference by a date certain and submit

 a discovery plan identifying unresolved disagreements. Ballentine Deel. 17; Ex. C-1. Plaintiff sent

 a separate email to counsel for Meta on the same date requesting Meta's position on the same

 subjects. Ballentine Deel. 17; Ex. C-2. Counsel for NCMEC and Hall replied the same day that

 counsel considered a Rule 26(f) conference premature because the pending motions, if granted in

 full, would dispose of all claims, because the surviving claims are not yet known, and because

 Plaintiff might seek leave to amend after a dismissal. Ballentine Deel. 1 8; Ex. C-1. The reply




                                                  2

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 105       Filed 10/28/26      Page 3 of 9 PageID#
                                              1072



 identified no order or other authority postponing the conference, proposed no date, and did not

 state whether NCMEC or Hall would oppose an order setting a conference deadline. Ex. C-1.

 Meta's counsel had not responded as of the execution of the accompanying Declaration. Ballentine

 Deel. ,-r 9.

          4.    The October 30, 2026 response date was requested by Plaintiff. It was not set by

 the Court. It had not passed when this Motion was filed. Plaintiff files now because the October

 28 reply states a position that planning should await the disposition of the motions to dismiss. That

 is a disagreement about timing that a prospective order can resolve. Plaintiff does not contend that

 any Defendant has defaulted on the October 30 date.

          5.    The Rule 26(f) conference has not been completed. Plaintiff has reviewed the

 docket through ECF 101 and has located no order expressly postponing the parties' Rule 26(f)

 conference. Ballentine Deel. ,-r 10.

          6.    A prospective order can resolve the timing dispute while preserving every party's

 substantive positions. The requested order directs participation and reporting. It does not require

 any party to agree with Plaintiffs proposals, and it permits each party to state in the report its

 position on dismissal, immunity, sequencing, phasing, and any requested postponement of

 discovery.

          7.    The requested dates can be coordinated with the separately requested Rule 16

 schedule. Plaintiff's Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order (ECF _) requests a Rule 16(b)

 scheduling conference within 21 days of the order granting it, with the parties' conference no later

 than seven days before and the report no later than three days before the Court's conference. The

 proposed order here provides that its deadlines govern unless another order expressly sets different




                                                  3

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF             Document 105        Filed 10/28/26      Page 4 of 9 PageID#
                                             1073



 conference or reporting dates, and that any coordinated dates are calculated from the Rule 16

 conference as actually scheduled.

 II.    SCOPE
        8.      This Motion seeks participation and reporting. It does not request adoption of

 Plaintiffs discovery proposals, answers to interrogatories, production of documents, sanctions, or

 modification of ECF 84. Plaintiffs pending objections and applications concerning ECF 84 and

 ECF 96 remain presented on their own grounds, and no request is withdrawn by this Motion.

        9.      This Motion does not depend on the disposition of Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of

 a Scheduling Order, and that motion does not depend on the disposition of this one.

 III.   LOCAL CIVIL RULE 37(E)
        10.     This Motion seeks prospective case-management directions under Rules 16 and

 26(f). It does not seek an order compelling disclosure or a response to a discovery request.

 Plaintiff's written efforts to obtain participation appear in the Declaration and Exhibits A through

 C-2. No telephone or in-person consultation concerning this request occurred. Plaintiff does not

 represent that the correspondence satisfies Local Civil Rule 37(E). If the Court determines that

 Local Civil Rule 37(E) applies, Plaintiff requests permission to proceed on that correspondence

 despite the absence of live consultation.

 IV.    RELIEF REQUESTED
        11.     Plaintiff requests that the Court enter the accompanying proposed order, which:

        (a)     directs Plaintiff and counsel for each appearing Defendant to complete the Rule

 26(f) conference no later than 14 days after entry of the order, by substantive written exchange on

 the subjects identified in Rule 26(±)(2)-(3) and Exhibit A § III, unless the Court directs otherwise;

        (b)     directs the parties to file the written discovery-plan report within 14 days after

 completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry of the order, unless the Court



                                                  4

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-WEF              Document 105         Filed 10/28/26      Page 5 of 9 PageID#
                                              1074



 expressly sets a different reporting deadline, stating the parties' agreed proposals and each party's

 separately attributed position on each subject in Rule 26(f)(3), including any requested sequencing,

 phasing, or postponement of discovery and any proposed protective or scheduling terms;

           (c)   provides that the report shall not portray any party's disagreement or silence as

 assent;

           (d)   provides that if the conference remains incomplete, the parties shall file a joint

 status report by the reporting deadline; that a party unable to obtain a joint report shall file its own

 report by that deadline; that each report shall identify the participation, exchanges, and remaining

 obstacle; and that a status report does not constitute completion of the conference, extend the

 completion deadline, or excuse further participation;

           (e)   shortens the preparatory intervals under Rule 26(f)(l), Rule 26(f)(4), and Local

 Civil Rule 26(A)(l) to the extent necessary to meet those dates;

           (f)   provides that the deadlines in the order govern unless another order expressly sets

 different conference or reporting dates; that any coordinated dates are calculated from the Rule

 16(b) conference as actually scheduled and remain achievable after entry; and that the pendency

 of Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order does not postpone compliance; and

           (g)   preserves all pending motions, defenses, objections, and existing orders except as

 the order expressly provides.

           12.   If the Court postpones the conference, Plaintiff requests that the order identify the

 scope of the postponement and a definite date or event for renewed consideration. These are

 requested case-management terms.

           13.   The proposed 14-day and 18-day periods are requested terms. The rules do not

 impose them.
